part.text: Empty repo. I'll scaffold a small Node.js project (ESM, zero dependencies, built-in test runner) with the range-to-regex core, a CLI, and tests.
Now tests. Write comprehensive brute-force test.

Wait, test "does not match leading zeros" — range 0-100, does `^(?:...)$` match "007"? Patterns include [0-9] which is single char, [1-9][0-9], [1-9], 100... "007" is 3 chars, no pattern matches 3 zero-leading. Good, false. "00" 2 chars: [1-9][0-9] requires first 1-9, no. false. Good.

Now run tests and lint.

part.text:
Everything works. Wait, the 500-5000 output: `[5-9][0-9]{2}` is 500-999, `1[0-9][0-9]{2}` is 1000-1999, `5000`, `[2-4][0-9]{3}` is 2000-4999. Correct. Ordering has 5000 before [2-4] but anchored so fine.

Done. Let me summarize concisely.

Project set up in `/work`:

- `package.json` — ESM, zero deps, `bin`, `test`/`lint` scripts
- `src/range-to-regex.js` — core: `rangeStringToRegex`, `rangeToRegex`, `rangeToRegexSource`, `parseRange`
- `src/cli.js` — `node src/cli.js 1-100` → `/^(?:[1-9]|[1-9][0-9]|100)$/`
- `test/range-to-regex.test.js` — 8 tests incl. exhaustive brute-force checks over 0–260

Run with `npm test`.
